<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **6** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 57574637129bebb4a6868c465be7e1b80eed1954` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `08ed6d7b0a6649d23ac1415cd56d4071f4a53309`
Local-runs: none

PR #20711, a draft onto `main` declaring itself part of #20678: 3 files, +423 / −24, base `defc7f7b5`, read as the net diff against `main` over refs fetched into this checkout's object store (a read, no worktree, nothing built or run). No governed path. Inputs: the card's body and its five comments (triage `5895784128`, claim `5897077531`, dev report `5898095119`, the seat's acceptance `5898156412`, retriage `5898181940`), the PR body and file list, and the head's check-runs. The dispatch order and the seat's own conclusions were not inputs; where this record agrees with them it is because the source agrees.

**Check-runs on the head, latest run per name, read 2026-09-29T20:38Z: 0 in progress, 0 failure.** All seven required contexts conclude `success`: `Lint & Repo Gates` (all `check:*` gates), `TypeScript Type Check`, `Test Core` (rollup and six shards), `Dogfood Regression Gate` (rollup and three shards), `Build Core`, `Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL)`, `Governed Surface Queue Guard`. Also `success`: `Check Changeset` on both runs (the job that runs `check-changeset-no-major` and `check-adr-0087-registration` with the PR body as input), `Dogfood Verify CLI`, the four `Type Check ·` jobs, `Part-of PR must not also close its card`, the two same-issue / single-writer claim checks, `Check Documentation Links`, `Flag docs affected by code changes`. `skipped` by design: `Console Pin Gate`, `Build Docs`, `Packed-tarball smoke (opt-in)`, and the second (post-relabel) runs of `Auto Label` and `Check PR Size`, whose first runs are `success`.

### ① Derived judgments

Read at source on the head: `engine.ts` (`subflowTargets`, `packagedSubflowCallers`, `disabledPackagedSubflows`, `ledgerDisabledChainReaches`, `refuseEnableOntoDisabledSubflow`, `toggleFlow`, `isFlowEnabled`), the declared-status passthrough in `packages/rest/src/error-response.ts`, the toggle arm in `packages/runtime/src/domains/automation.ts`, `isCodeArtifactBody` in `packages/metadata-core`, and ADR-0126 §7.2 / §7.3 / §9.

1. **The `toggleFlow(name, true)` accept set NARROWS — right.** A packaged caller the ledger holds off is refused when a packaged `subflow` or `map` target is not `isFlowEnabled`. The guard runs before `flowActivationStore.setActive`, so a refusal moves nothing; the pins assert the row, the binding and `execute()` after the refusal.
2. **The `toggleFlow(name, false)` accept set is UNCHANGED — right.** `packagedSubflowCallers` is re-expressed over `subflowTargets`; the old predicate `n.config?.flowName === name` and the new `subflowTargets(flow).includes(name)` (string-typed `flowName` only) are equivalent for a string `name`. The disable refusal's text, envelope (`DELETE_RESTRICTED` / 409) and `subflowCallers` key are untouched. The card's own reproduction therefore still fails on this branch, and the PR body says so in as many words.
3. **The wire — right.** `POST /api/v1/automation/:name/toggle` with `enabled: true` gains a `409 RESOURCE_CONFLICT` answer. The route calls `toggleFlow` and lets the throw reach the dispatcher; the REST layer's declared-status passthrough (a numeric `status` on the thrown error, a catalog-member `code`) is what carries `{code: RESOURCE_CONFLICT, httpStatus: 409}` to the client with no route change, and the dev's live reading agrees with that source. `RESOURCE_CONFLICT` is a standard-catalog 409 member (`packages/spec/src/api/errors.zod.ts`), so no ADR-0112 ledger entry is minted, and `IJobService.replay()` is the in-repo precedent for the same member. The hand-written error catalog page's `RESOURCE_CONFLICT` entry stays accurate (generic "conflicts with current state"); its 409 quick-reference row lists "common codes", not an exhaustive set. The Docs Drift comment is advisory, and no hand-written page states the guard's direction (the refusal prose has 0 hits under `content/docs`).
4. **No public-surface change — right.** All four new engine members are `private`; `IAutomationService.toggleFlow?` in `packages/spec` is unchanged; no export, spec key, route, query parameter or env var moves. `check:api-surface` has nothing to see, and `TypeScript Type Check` is green.
5. **"Packaged" is decided by `describeFlowContender` → `isCodeArtifactBody` (a truthy `_packageId`, not the `sys_metadata` sentinel, not tenant-authored) — right.** The two control pins (`_packageId: undefined`) exercise the real discriminator, the same one the disable-direction pins already use.
6. **The cycle exemption — right as declared, with one unpinned corner (③.4).** `ledgerDisabledChainReaches` walks only ledger-disabled packaged links, and the caller is already known ledger-disabled, so a loop it finds is one every enable order would refuse; the chain-through-an-enabled-flow pin proves the walk stops at an enabled link, and a status-disabled link never closes the loop because publishing re-arms it through a door this guard does not sit on.
7. **The remedy follows the child's real state — right.** The switch moves only the ledger bit, so a status-disabled child gets the publish remedy, and the pin proves the toggle remedy would have been a dead end (`toggleFlow(child, true)` lands and `execute()` still answers `FLOW_DISABLED`).
8. **ADR-0126 is extended, not reversed — right.** §7.3 is headed "attached to disable" and records why the disable guard exists; it does not decide that enable is unguarded (the sentence "Enable is never guarded" was a code comment, not ADR text), and §9's not-chartered list does not name an enable guard. The enable direction applies §7.3's own rationale (a vendor flow failing late at its subflow node) from the other end. No new ADR is owed by this PR; ③.5 names the addendum line it leaves owed.
9. **Test order and ablations — read from the commit list, not re-run.** `73333a32c` (pins, red first) → `58f0aef61` (fix) → `08ed6d7b0` (changeset). The nine ablation legs and the live boot are the dev's readings, consistent with the code, and are taken as such under `Local-runs: none`; the `Test Core` shards are the gate verdict on the pins.
10. **The dead-reader claim — right.** The `DELETE_RESTRICTED` arm relays `developerMessage`, `dependentObject` and `dependentCount` only, so `subflowCallers` never reaches the wire; the enable refusal adding no parallel key is the consistent choice, and the message names the flows.

### ② Semver level

- **The changeset** `.changeset/20678-subflow-disable-sequence.md` grades `@objectstack/service-automation` `minor`, carries a **BREAKING** banner, the `no (narrowing)` declaration, and exactly one ADR-0087 marker, `not-required (no-migration-prescription)`. The package is published (`17.5.0`, not private), so a changeset is owed and `skip-changeset` would have been wrong.
- **The `Clause-②` declaration — `no (narrowing)` is RIGHT; the claim line's `yes` was wrong.** Per `scripts/pm/clause2-line.mjs` the value answers only whether the card widens an accept set or the public surface; this diff widens nothing (①.1–①.4) and narrows the enable accept set, which is the arm's own case: "NOT a widening, but breaking. This is the whole point of the arm." The claim's `yes` reasoned from both halves of the card, and only the narrowing half landed. The PR body's line 2 and the changeset carry the same declaration, as the post-task checklist requires.
- **The level — `minor` is RIGHT; the order's `patch` was wrong.** AGENTS.md: `(narrowing)` is BREAKING; during the launch window a breaking change ships `minor` (`check-changeset-no-major.mjs`, whose header carries the end condition at GA), and its level axis reads `no (narrowing)` as owing at least `minor` on a moved package. `no (narrowing)` with `patch` refuses by construction, and so does `yes` with `patch`. `Check Changeset` concluded `success` on this head.
- **The migration text — RIGHT for this shape.** Nothing an author writes is removed or renamed, so no FROM → TO mapping and no tombstone is owed; the body states what is now refused, the envelope, and the two operator remedies. `no-migration-prescription` holds because those are operator steps, not consumer code rewrites, which is the one thing that category is refused on.
- The two errors the seat corrected on the card in `5898156412` — the claim's `yes` and the retired `needs:contract-review` label — are corrected in fact: the PR carries `documentation`, `size/m`, `tests`, `tooling` only.

### ③ Boundary flags

1. **The disable half not built (deviation 1, open question 1) — ESCALATED, correctly.** Premise A1 was measured false: `resume()` and `resumeInternal()` never consult `isFlowEnabled`, in three shapes including the shipped map pair's own. The dispatch's fork rule fired, and the choice (options A–D, the seat recommends A) sits on the card as `pm:retriage` in `5898181940` beside `pm:dispatched`. The PR declares itself part of the card rather than closing it, and the body states that the reproduction is unchanged. **As the enable half alone the PR is sound and honest:** it is self-contained, the disable behaviour is the old predicate re-expressed, and every sentence about the half not built is labelled as such.
2. **The declaration and level deviation (deviation 2, open question 2) — ANSWERED:** keep as delivered (② above; the seat's reading in `5898156412` agrees).
3. **The `registerFlow` door (out-of-scope finding 1) — noted, unfiled; carry forward.** A package upgrade, publish or hot reload can still arm a packaged caller onto a disabled child; the guard sits on `toggleFlow` only, and the pins build their state through exactly that door. Unfiled for want of a measured repro through a public door, which is acceptable under Prime Directive #10 as an acceptance note. The retriage answer for the disable half should say whether the chosen option also covers registration, because option A (parked-run reachability) and option B (resume refusal) reach that door differently.
4. **A child disabled BOTH ways inside a ledger-disabled cycle is skipped whole:** in `disabledPackagedSubflows` the cycle `continue` runs before the status half is read, so the completable publish remedy is not named and the caller is armed onto a status-disabled child. Declared, since the changeset's "Not refused" list covers a subflow in a cycle of switched-off flows; unpinned; a corner of a corner and not blocking. Carry into the disable-half stage beside 3.
5. **ADR-0126 §7.3 now under-describes the guard** ("attached to disable"). Not a reversal (①.8), so no ADR is owed by this PR; one addendum sentence naming the enable direction is owed on `docs/adr/` — Tier H, the maintainer's hand — at the latest with the disable half.
6. **A status-disabled caller judged on its ledger re-enable (out-of-scope finding 3) — noted; the named remedy completes.** A boundary, not a defect.
7. **`subflowCallers` unread on the disable refusal (out-of-scope finding 2) — noted; zero pull.**
8. **UI rendering of the new 409 on the Setup packaged-automation board — NOT MEASURED, declared.** The board renders the server message (the acceptance run on #20674); no route or body shape changed.
9. **Base drift:** `main` has moved 5 commits since base `defc7f7b5` (the body names the first 3). Measured over the fetched refs, none touches `packages/services/service-automation`, the automation domain, `error-response.ts` or the error catalog. The queue's merge-ref build is the second CI round.
10. **Hygiene:** 3 files only, no probe file, no `.md` outside `.changeset/`, no model identifier in title, body, changeset or code. Both refusal messages cite the ADR by id (the disable text is the precedent), and `Lint & Repo Gates` is green.
